topic: An artist discovers someone has tattooed their work
text: Rain was drumming on the cheap tin roof of the studio as I studied the canvases, the colors now permanent under someone's skin. This wasn't just a job, not when the lines of a man's face were etched alongside the strokes of an artist’s brush. I ran a hand through my hair, the weight of the room pressing down on me. The artist had been calm when they showed me the proof, a phone buzzing with alerts that couldn’t be ignored. But there was something in their eyes, a spark that had dimmed. I knew that look too well, the kind that comes when you've lost more than just a piece of art. Contracts, rights, it all fades to static when you're staring at a canvas that’s become a stranger's flesh. I had to fix this, not just for the money, but because some things, once broken, don't mend easily.
